summary.headline: Astral Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR 1,988 crore with EBITDA margin of 13.7%, while H1 plumbing volume grew 10.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 1,988 crore, with EBITDA of INR 272 crore (13.7% margin). Plumbing delivered INR 1,398 crore (+25%) with 16.3% EBITDA margin, while adhesives India, adhesives UK and paints grew 25%, 30% and 44% respectively, but adhesives and paints margins were under pressure from high-cost inventory and lagged price pass-through. Management said October was the best month in company history and guided to a stronger H2 for plumbing, targeting roughly INR 1,050 crore plumbing EBITDA and about INR 1,250 crore group EBITDA for FY27.

guidance_outlook: Plumbing: double-digit volume growth guided; H2 expected to exceed H1 (10.1%). Full-year plumbing volume targeted at about 290,000-300,000 tonnes.
Plumbing EBITDA: full-year plumbing EBITDA of about INR 1,050 crore projected (H1 INR 426 crore, 40/60 split assumed as last year). Plumbing margin guidance of 16-18% reaffirmed; H1 was 17.4%.
Group EBITDA: about INR 1,250 crore projected for FY27, including about INR 200 crore plus from chemicals (DSS and others); FY28 EBITDA growth of about 15% indicated.
Adhesives India: full-year EBITDA guidance of 14-15%; management now expects about 13-14% run rate by year-end and full-year near 13%. Revenue growth guidance to be raised above prior 15-20%.
Adhesives UK: targets 9-10% EBITDA margin; year-end margins to return to normal levels.
Paints: guided positive EBITDA of about 3-4% by year-end and 8-10% next year; no new geographies until EBITDA reaches about 9-10% in existing states; growth run-rate target of 40-50%.

Capex: FY27 capex expected at about INR 400 crore including Nexelon CPVC plant (about INR 40 crore) and goodwill-related items; INR 260 crore spent in H1. Sale of Bengaluru asset from Gem Paints expected to bring about INR 50-52 crore.
capex_capacity: Plastic plumbing capacity stated at 425 KT (press release).
CPVC backward integration plant (Nexelon) construction nearly complete; trials expected in first month of Q4 FY27 and commercial readiness by last month of Q4.
PEX and aluminium PEX machinery installed and stabilised; commercial sales from own plant expected from Q3 FY27.
Management said land and buildings are in place to add about 100 KT in 6-9 months; 60-70% of capex cost is land and building, already in hand.
Kanpur plant opened recently; further capacity possible at Hyderabad and other plants. CPVC ramp-up expected to take up to one quarter.
demand_pricing: October was described as the best month in Astral's history across products, with unprecedented plumbing demand; management expects double-digit momentum in Q3 and Q4.
Industry Q1 was weak with low trade inventory, which drove the Q2 rebound; the industry priced up with a lag.
MIP (minimum import price) implemented; management sees a base price of about INR 85-90/kg protecting the downside, with countervailing duty under consideration.
CPVC price hike of 5% taken in October; PVC price increases since September fully passed through.
Adhesives India: H1 growth is mostly volume-led, with rural, online and overseas expansion; Q3 and Q4 top-line growth expected to match the Q1-Q2 run rate.
Sanitary ware is part of plumbing and estimated at around breakeven plus a small positive EBITDA.
Payable days fell as the company paid dollar liabilities early to avoid forex losses; inventory held on average 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for plumbing in H2 and whether 12-13% is possible given the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Kairav said October was unprecedented and expects double-digit momentum into Q3 and Q4; full-year volume target is 290,000-300,000 tonnes, with no specific growth figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 margins per kg fall versus Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a scheme-driven pipe-heavy mix in September, a PVC-heavy quarter, and lagged price pass-through by the industry were the reasons; CPVC and value-added mix are expected to be better in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will adhesive India and UK guidance be upgraded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adhesive India growth guidance will be 'much higher' than the earlier 15%, with no exact figure; UK margin is expected to improve gradually to 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory and payable days move?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose from inflation; Sept 30 figures are a point-in-time read, and average holding is 55-60 days. Payables fell due to early payment of dollar liabilities to avoid forex losses, which management says is a current-environment decision.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the paint margin improvement and what is the path to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 40-50% growth run-rate, overhead absorption and lower manpower, warehousing and delivery costs; collections are now 60 days after legacy Gem Paints issues, and no bad debts are reported.

qa_highlights.question: Overhead cost trend and when it will decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-quarter overhead realisation was about INR 190 (per kg) and expects over INR 200 in the next quarter; OpEx rose 19-20% YoY in H1 against revenue growth of 26%.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility: management attributes margin pressure to high-cost inventory and lagged pass-through; crude moves are the key swing factor.
Full-year plumbing EBITDA of about INR 1,050 crore depends on H2 contributing about 60%, which management says follows a historical pattern.
Adhesives margin gap: India at 11.5% H1 versus 14-15% guidance; UK at 5.6% H1 versus 9-10% target.
Paints remain EBITDA-negative in H1; management has not opened new states until margins reach 9-10%.
CPVC plant commissioning and ramp-up timeline (trials in Q4 FY27) and PEX launch in Q3.
Working capital: lower payable days and rising inventory days, which may reverse once currency stabilises.
Inconsistent reporting of paint growth (39.9% vs 43.9%) and of some figures on the call, which may need verification against the press release.
key_quotes: I think October we saw unprecedented demand and the sale has been very good.
Definitely there will be an upper side, much upper side, I can say, rather than what 15% we have given.

We assure you, and we are very much conscious about bringing this EBITDA margin back to the normal level in this quarter, and by the end of this fiscal year, again, to the margins of 13%, 14%, or up to 15%.
Now, whether we will deliver 10% or 11% or 12%, that still is to be seen.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year plumbing and group EBITDA targets and on volume momentum, with October described as unprecedented. Noticeably cautious on adhesives and paints margins, which management attributes to high-cost inventory, lagged price pass-through and crude volatility, and it repeatedly deferred specific growth or margin numbers to "much higher" or "around" language.
